title: LiveWorld — Small world. Big what if.
disclosures: Actual application UI captures and native simulation replay exports
Recorded Meta outputs labelled and recomputed

scenes.heading: One bridge. Every home on time.
scenes.caption: Recorded Meta study · same six couriers, demand and deadlines
scenes.narration: One moved bridge. Every home supplied on time. LiveWorld turns a small game world into an experiment, with changes you can see and results you can verify.

scenes.heading: Objects become a design language
scenes.caption: AI-generated tabletop test input · not a real camera capture
scenes.narration: A cup becomes a well, blocks become homes, and sticks become bridges. This tabletop image is generated.

scenes.heading: Meaning, shape, then your confirmation
scenes.caption: Actual Muse Spark + SAM response · inference waiting time omitted
scenes.narration: Muse Spark proposes the objects and their roles. SAM traces their shapes. These are actual returned masks. The creator reviews the suggestions before the image-relative positions become a fixed-grid level.

scenes.heading: A connected world can still miss its deadlines
scenes.caption: Authored valley challenge · 20/24 water units arrive on time
scenes.narration: Now switch to an authored challenge. Six couriers supply six homes, each with its own deadline. Everything is connected, yet four water units arrive late. Movement, stock, queues and deadlines are computed by the simulator.

scenes.heading: A good-sounding idea must survive a test
scenes.caption: Recorded Meta trial · balanced dispatch: 20/24 → 14/24
scenes.narration: Balanced dispatch sounds like a reasonable fix. In this recorded Meta experiment, it makes the outcome worse: only fourteen of twenty-four units arrive on time. The simulator rejects the hypothesis. Model confidence cannot change that result.

scenes.heading: Change the crossing. Keep the constraints.
scenes.caption: Recorded Meta study · 24/24 on time · waiting increases 16 → 22 turns
scenes.narration: The playtester uses simulation tools to investigate allowed edits. Its search includes a systematic sweep; that part is code, not invented reasoning. Moving the south bridge gets every unit there on time, with the same workers, demand and deadlines. Waiting increases, so the tradeoff remains visible.

scenes.heading: Change the rules. See what follows.
scenes.caption: Recorded Meta rule proposal · north bridge closed on turns 25–50
scenes.narration: Creators can design a different challenge: close the north bridge from turn twenty-five through fifty. Muse Spark compiles that instruction into a validated schedule. The bridge really closes, couriers reroute, and on-time delivery falls from twenty to sixteen. This is a creator design change, separate from a same-resource repair.

scenes.heading: Useful evidence includes an unfinished answer
scenes.caption: Recorded Meta playtest under the closure · 16/24 → 22/24 · not solved
scenes.narration: Under that new schedule, another recorded Meta playtest improves delivery from sixteen to twenty-two. The closure remains locked. Some deadlines are still missed, and the app says so. A bounded search is useful evidence, not proof that every level is solved.

scenes.heading: Keep the experiment, not just the animation
scenes.caption: Portable project · recomputed results · 1080p replay export
scenes.narration: Save the world, checkpoints and trials as a portable project. Reopening validates the inputs and recomputes the measurements. Export an inspectable report or a smooth replay clip directly from the product. These local replays need no API calls, so a collaborator can examine the same experiment.

scenes.heading: Small world. Big what if.
scenes.caption: Built by Tang Vu · powered by Meta · github.com/tang-vu/liveworld
scenes.narration: LiveWorld is a tabletop playtest studio for small logistics games. It connects design intent to an executable system, a visible failure, and a measured change. The prototype uses a fixed grid and two timed mechanics. The next step is testing this workflow with game creators.
